title: The Middle and Passive Participles
subtitle: λυόμενος, λυσάμενος, λυθείς — middle and passive forms.
objectives: Form and decline the present and aorist middle participles.
Form and decline the aorist passive participle.
Distinguish middle from passive participles by context.
Translate middle and passive participles correctly.

sections.heading: Middle and passive participles
sections.body:
The present and aorist middle participles follow the same declension pattern as the active, but with middle endings. The present middle/passive participle is λυόμενος, λυομένη, λυόμενον. The aorist middle participle is λυσάμενος, λυσαμένη, λυσάμενον.

The aorist passive participle has its own form: λυθείς, λυθεῖσα, λυθέν. This is the first time you have seen a separate passive form. The aorist passive participle uses the θη infix (you will learn the full aorist passive system in Stage 4).

sections.heading: The present middle/passive participle: λυόμενος, λυομένη, λυόμενον
sections.body:
Masculine:
              singular        plural
  nominative  λυόμενος        λυόμενοι
  genitive    λυομένου        λυομένων
  dative      λυομένῳ         λυομένοις
  accusative  λυόμενον        λυομένους

Feminine:
              singular        plural
  nominative  λυομένη         λυόμεναι
  genitive    λυομένης        λυομένων
  dative      λυομένῃ         λυομέναις
  accusative  λυομένην        λυομένας

Neuter:
              singular        plural
  nominative  λυόμενον        λυόμενα
  genitive    λυομένου        λυομένων
  dative      λυομένῳ         λυομένοις
  accusative  λυόμενον        λυόμενα

This follows the first and second declension pattern: masculine and neuter like ἀγαθός, feminine like ἀγαθή.

sections.heading: The aorist middle participle: λυσάμενος, λυσαμένη, λυσάμενον
sections.body:
The aorist middle participle follows the same declension as the present middle, but with the aorist stem λυσα-.

λυσάμενος means 'having freed himself' or 'having freed (for himself)'.

The pattern is identical to λυόμενος.

sections.heading: The aorist passive participle: λυθείς, λυθεῖσα, λυθέν
sections.body:
Masculine:
              singular        plural
  nominative  λυθείς          λυθέντες
  genitive    λυθέντος        λυθέντων
  dative      λυθέντι         λυθεῖσι(ν)
  accusative  λυθέντα         λυθέντας

Feminine:
              singular        plural
  nominative  λυθεῖσα         λυθεῖσαι
  genitive    λυθείσης        λυθεισῶν
  dative      λυθείσῃ         λυθείσαις
  accusative  λυθεῖσαν        λυθείσας

Neuter:
              singular        plural
  nominative  λυθέν           λυθέντα
  genitive    λυθέντος        λυθέντων
  dative      λυθέντι         λυθεῖσι(ν)
  accusative  λυθέν           λυθέντα

The stem is λυθεντ-. The θη infix marks the aorist passive.

items.answer: genitive singular masculine or neuter of λυόμενος
genitive singular masculine or neuter of λυσάμενος
genitive singular masculine or neuter of λυθείς

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.13 introduces the genitive absolute. The genitive absolute is a participial phrase in the genitive case, grammatically independent of the main sentence. It is one of the most elegant constructions in Greek.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can form and decline the present middle, aorist middle, and aorist passive participles of any ω-verb.
